source_text: τετειχισμένην, καὶ ταῖς ἄνωθεν ἐπικουρίαις διεζωσμένην, καὶ φρένας ἔχοντες ἀστικὰς, καὶ τὸ τῷ Θεῷ δοκοῦν οὐκ ἠγνοηκότες, εἶτα τοῦ πρέποντος ἀλογήσαντες, τὸν σφίσιν αὐτοῖς ἀπονεμηθέντα κλῆρον ἀποβεβληκότες ἐκ ῥᾳθυμίας, καὶ τῆς ἄγαν ἐλπίδος ἐκπεπτωκότες, εἰ μὴ ἐκνήψειαν ἂν ἐκ μέθης αὐτῶν, κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον, καὶ ἀνακομίσαιντο τὰ οἰκεῖα, τοῦ τῆς λυτρώσεως ἐνεστηκότος ἐνιαυτοῦ, τοῦτ' ἔστι, τῆς τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν ἐπιδημίας, ἀπομενοῦσι λοιπὸν, καὶ διηνεκῶς ὑποκείσονται τῷ πριαμένῳ, τοῦτ' ἔστι τῷ Σατανᾷ. «Ἰδοὺ γὰρ, φησὶ, ταῖς ἀνομίαις ὑμῶν ἐπράθητε, καὶ ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ὑμῶν ἐξαπέστειλα τὴν μητέρα ὑμῶν.» Ἀνεπικούρητος δὲ παντελῶς ἡ τῶν ἐθνῶν οὖσα πληθὺς, καὶ τὴν ἄγροικόν τε καὶ ἀμαθῆ νοσοῦσα φρένα, ταύτῃτοι καὶ ἐξωσμένη πρὸς τὴν ὑφ' ἑτέροις δουλείαν, λυτρωτὴ διὰ παντός ἐστιν, ἐποικτείροντος τοῦ Θεοῦ· ἀναλήψεται γὰρ τὸν ἴδιον κλῆρον κεκλημένη πρὸς ἐλευθερίαν, ἐν τῷ ἔτει τῆς ἀφέσεως, ὅτε πᾶσαν τὴν ὑφ' ἡλίῳ τῆς τῶν δαιμονίων πλεονεξίας ἀνῆκε Χριστὸς, καὶ τῶν τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἐξείλετο βρόχων, καὶ δεδικαίωκεν ἐν πίστει, καὶ ἡγίακεν ἐν πνεύματι, καταργήσας τῷ ἰδίῳ σταυρῷ τὸ καθ' ἡμῶν χειρόγραφον, ἀνεκποίητα δὲ τὰ Λευϊτικά· τετήρηται γὰρ ἀσφαλῶς τοῖς ἁγίοις ὁ κλῆρος, καὶ ἐρηρεισμένην ἔχουσι τὴν ἐλπίδα. Καὶ γοῦν ἐπὶ τῇ φιλομαθεστάτῃ Μαριὰμ ἔφη που Χριστὸς, ὅτι τὴν καλὴν μερίδα ἐξελέξατο, ἥτις οὐκ ἀφαιρεθήσεται ἀπ' αὐτῆς. Πλὴν μικροῦ καὶ μεγάλου ἱερέως καὶ λαοῦ, καὶ πάντων τῶν ἁπαξαπλῶς ἡ λύτρωσις ἐν Χριστῷ καὶ τὸ τῆς ἐλπίδος ἀσφαλές. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀπεμπωλήσει δὴ οὖν τὸν ἴδιον κλῆρον ὁ Ἰσραὴλ, τῆς λυτρώσεως τὸν ἐνιαυτὸν οὐκ ἐπεγνωκώς· ἔσται γε μὴν ἐν καθέξει τῆς ἐλπίδος τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ τῶν τῆς φύσεως ἀγαθῶν ἐπανάληψις ἔσται διὰ Χριστοῦ. {ΚΥΡ.} Οὕτω φημί· κατασφραγιεῖ δὲ τὸν λόγον ἡμῶν εἰς τὸ ἀληθὲς, ὁ τῶν ὅλων Θεὸς καὶ καθ' ἕτερον τοῦτο σημαίνων τρόπον, διὰ φωνῆς Ἰεζεχιὴλ, ἐν τῇ τοῦ οἴκου διαμετρήσει· «Τάδε λέγει Κύριος· Ἐὰν δῷ ὁ ἀφηγούμενος δόμα ἑνὶ ἐκ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτοῦ, ἐκ τῆς κληρονομίας αὐτοῦ, τοῦτο τοῖς υἱοῖς αὐτοῦ ἔσται· ἢ ἑνὶ τῶν παίδων αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔσται αὐτῷ ἕως τοῦ ἔτους τῆς ἀφέσεως. Καὶ ἀποδώσει τῷ ἀφηγουμένῳ, πλὴν τῆς κληρονομίας τῶν υἱῶν αὐτοῦ αὐτοῖς ἔσται, καὶ οὐ μὴ λάβῃ ὁ ἀφηγούμενος ἐκ τῆς κληρονομίας τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτοῦ καταδυναστεῦσαι αὐτοὺς ἐκ τῆς κατασχέσεως αὐτοῦ, ἀπὸ κληρονομίας αὐτοῦ κατακληρονομῆσαι τοῖς υἱοῖς αὐτοῦ, ὅπως μὴ διασκορπίζηται ὁ λαός μου, ἕκαστος ἀπὸ κατασχέσεως αὐτοῦ.» Ἆρά σοι σαφὲς τὸ χρησμῴδημα, καὶ ψιλὸς ὁρᾶται τῆς ἱστορίας ὁ νοῦς; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Οὐδαμῶς· ἀναμάθοιμι δ' ἂν ὡς ἥδιστά γε. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἡγούμενον, ὦ Παλλάδιε, τὸν ἀρχιερέα καλεῖ, τὸν καθηγεῖσθαι λαχόντα τῶν ὑπὸ χεῖρα λαῶν. Οὐκοῦν ἐπειδήπερ ἐπιτήδειοι καὶ ἐξαίρετοι τοῖς ἁγίοις
pass_a_gloss: [Cyril, continuing from §14: 'So the Jews, dwelling in a city'] walled, girded with the helps from above, having city dwellers' minds, not ignorant of what seems good to God, then neglecting the fitting, having thrown away the lot allotted to them out of slackness, having fallen from the great hope; unless they should sober up from their drunkenness as written, and recover their own while the year of redemption is present, that is, the sojourn/coming of our Saviour, they will remain thereafter and be perpetually subject to the buyer, that is, Satan. Isa 50:1 quoted: behold, by your lawlessnesses you were sold, by your sins I sent away your mother. The multitude of the nations, altogether helpless, sick with the rustic and unlearned mind, therefore thrust out into slavery under others, is redeemable always, God pitying; for, called to freedom, it will take back its own lot in the year of release, when Christ released all under the sun from the greed of the demons, took it out of the nooses of sin, justified in faith, sanctified in the Spirit, having abolished by his own cross the handwriting against us. But the Levitical things are inalienable: the lot is kept securely for the saints, and they have the hope fixed. Thus of most learning loving Mary Christ said she chose the good portion which will not be taken from her. Yet of small and great, priest and people, and all simply, the redemption in Christ and the security of hope. PALL.: Israel will sell off its lot, not having recognized the year of redemption; the nations will be in possession of hope, and there will be a taking back of nature's goods through Christ. CYR.: So I say; the God of all will seal our word as true, signifying it another way, through Ezekiel's voice, in the measurement of the house: Ezek 46:16-18 quoted ('the leader', gift, inheritance, servant, oppress, possession, give as inheritance, scatter). Is the oracle clear to you and is the sense of the history seen bare? PALL.: Not at all; I would most gladly learn. CYR.: He calls the high priest 'leader', Palladius, the one allotted to lead the peoples under hand. Since then suitable and choice lots have been assigned to the holy [ministers, §16]…
pass_b_english: Cyril: …that is walled and girded about with help from above, who have the minds of townsfolk and have not been ignorant of what pleases God, but then disregarded what was fitting, have thrown away through carelessness the lot assigned to them and have fallen from their high hope: unless they sober up from their drunkenness, as it is written (Joel 1:5), and recover what is their own while the year of redemption is here (Leviticus 25:29–30), that is, the coming of our Savior, they will be left as they are from then on and will be subject forever to the buyer, that is, to Satan. ‘For behold,’ he says, ‘you were sold for your iniquities, and for your sins I sent away your mother’ (Isaiah 50:1). But the multitude of the nations, wholly without help and sick with a rustic and untaught mind, and for that reason driven out into slavery under others, can be redeemed at any time (Leviticus 25:31), because God takes pity on it. For it will take back its own lot, called to freedom in the year of release, when Christ set free all the earth under the sun from the greed of the demons, rescued it from the snares of sin, justified it by faith and sanctified it in the Spirit, canceling by his own cross the bond that stood against us (Colossians 2:14). The possessions of the Levites, however, can never be sold off (Leviticus 25:32–34); for the lot is kept safe for the saints, and their hope stands firm. So it was that Christ once said of Mary, who was so very eager to learn, that she had chosen the good portion, which will not be taken away from her (Luke 10:42). Yet for small and great, for priest and people, and in a word for all, redemption and the security of hope are in Christ.

Palladius: So Israel will sell off its own lot, because it did not recognize the year of redemption; but the nations will possess the hope, and the good things of nature will be regained through Christ.

Cyril: So I say. And the God of all will seal our account as true, showing this also in another way through the voice of Ezekiel, in the measuring of the house: ‘Thus says the Lord: If the leader gives a gift to one of his sons out of his inheritance, it shall belong to his sons. But if he gives it to one of his servants, it shall be his until the year of release, and he shall give it back to the leader; only the inheritance of his sons shall remain theirs. And the leader shall not take any of the inheritance of his people, to oppress them and drive them from their possession, and from his inheritance to give an inheritance to his sons, so that my people may not be scattered, each from his own possession’ (Ezekiel 46:16–18). Is the oracle clear to you, and does the sense of the history stand out plainly?
Palladius: Not at all; but I would most gladly learn.
Cyril: By ‘leader,’ Palladius, he means the high priest, the one whose lot it is to lead the peoples under his hand. Since, then, fitting and select lots have been assigned to the holy…

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 13 to compare. Sense taken from the PG 68 Greek. The withheld earlier English was not used as a model.

apparatus.note: Opens mid-sentence: §14 ends 'Cyril: So the Jews, who dwell in a city…' (πόλιν… τετειχισμένην); English continues that turn. Cyril is still expounding the house-redemption law of Leviticus 25:29–34 (walled-city houses redeemable only within a year; village houses always redeemable and released at the jubilee; Levites' houses always redeemable and their fields never sold); inline citations to Leviticus 25 mark these clear allusions, not quotations. 'As it is written' with ἐκνήψειαν… ἐκ μέθης: no exact verse; Joel 1:5 LXX (ἐκνήψατε, οἱ μεθύοντες, ἐξ οἴνου αὐτῶν) is the closest and is cited, but the wording is loose (cf. 1 Corinthians 15:34 ἐκνήψατε). Isaiah 50:1 quoted with ἀνομίαις/ἁμαρτίαις in reverse order to the usual LXX text. 'Called to freedom' may echo Galatians 5:13 (uncited). 'Did not recognize the year' may echo Luke 19:44 (uncited). 'Small and great, priest and people' left uncited (possible echo of Isaiah 24:2). Ezekiel 46:16–18 as Cyril quotes it differs from standard LXX: omits κατάσχεσις in v.16 and reads ἀπὸ κληρονομίας αὐτοῦ κατακληρονομῆσαι τοῖς υἱοῖς αὐτοῦ in v.18; 'his inheritance' kept ambiguous as in the Greek; Cyril's later gloss (§17) takes the clause as 'take from the people's inheritance to give to his sons'. παῖς in v.17 = servant (Cyril glosses οἰκέτης in §16). ἀφηγούμενος/ἡγούμενος both rendered 'leader'. Section ends mid-sentence ('the holy…'), continued in §16 ('…ministers').

review.method: translate from the Greek, then a separate clause-by-clause review against the Greek
changes: Opening rebuilt as one grammatical sentence continuing §14 'So the Jews, who dwell in a city…' (old text left §14's subject without a verb); participle tenses kept
ἐνεστηκότος: 'is at hand' -> 'is here' (present, not approaching)
πᾶσαν τὴν ὑφ' ἡλίῳ: 'whole world' -> 'all the earth under the sun'
ἀνεκποίητα: 'cannot be sold away' -> 'can never be sold off'
φιλομαθεστάτῃ: superlative restored ('so very eager to learn')
Palladius: ἐν καθέξει 'hold fast to' -> 'possess'; τῆς φύσεως 'our nature' -> 'nature' (no added 'our'); ἐπανάληψις 'restored' -> 'regained'
ψιλὸς ὁρᾶται τῆς ἱστορίας ὁ νοῦς: fixed misattached 'bare history' -> 'does the sense of the history stand out plainly?'
καθ' ἕτερον ... τρόπον: 'in yet another way' -> 'also in another way'; ἐπιτήδειοι: 'special' -> 'fitting'; 'allotments' -> 'lots' (consistency)

Scripture checked: Joel 1:5 (LXX ἐκνήψατε... ἐξ οἴνου αὐτῶν, closest to 'as it is written'), Leviticus 25:29-34, Isaiah 50:1 (Cyril's word order kept), Colossians 2:14, Luke 10:42, Ezekiel 46:16-18 all confirmed
